dedupe_keys.name: usgs quantitative risk of earthquake disruption to the global copper and rhenium supply chain ofr 2024 1028

description: A USGS study that estimates how often earthquakes disrupt the world's copper and rhenium supply. Open-File Report 2024-1028 combines global earthquake hazard models with the locations of copper mines, smelters and refineries and estimates the expected share of capacity disrupted each year: 0.3 to 1.1 per cent for mines, 1.8 to 4.0 per cent for smelters and 1.5 to 3.3 per cent for refineries, with 0.32 to 1.32 per cent for rhenium, a by-product of copper. It puts expected annual lost revenue at 315 million to 1.29 billion US dollars for mining, 1.92 to 4.33 billion for smelting and 2.06 to 4.52 billion for refining. The report is a free downloadable publication. Coverage is global facilities. Caveats: results rest on facility lists and fragility assumptions stated in the report, and ranges reflect that uncertainty. For simulation it shows how to turn hazard models and facility inventories into expected supply loss for a critical mineral, a template for other commodities. A related catalogue record is the USGS global critical minerals mines, deposits and districts dataset.
